The upward (post-order) pass has the same problem as any tree DP: depth 2e5 on a path-shaped tree against a ~1e4 JavaScript cap, no raisable limit. The downward pass is worse: it carries a value from parent to child, so the explicit-stack rewrite must push the parent's contribution onto the stack alongside the vertex, whereas the recursion carried it implicitly in the frame as an argument. The C++ default writes both passes as plain recursion and never confronts this. In JavaScript both passes must be rewritten with explicit stacks, and the downward one's per-frame payload must be made explicit — a genuine acquisition, at exactly the tree sizes rerooting is FOR (rerooting exists to avoid the O(n^2) of re-running the DP from every root, so it is only reached for when n is large — precisely where the JavaScript stack fails).
docs/research/C005-dp-map-package/01_cross-reference-view.md:5764: - MATERIAL AND BLOCKING — the flagship recursion finding of this audit. This node writes the post-order DFS, and the post-order DFS is exactly the shape JavaScript cannot run at competitive sizes. C++'s recursive post-order on a tree of n = 2e5 reaches depth 2e5 on a path-shaped tree; a typical 8 MB stack absorbs it and some judges raise the limit further, platform-dependent. JavaScript throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded at a depth on the order of 1e4 — an order of magnitude BELOW the input sizes this technique routinely meets — and a submitted program cannot raise the limit. So the recursive realization is not slow in JavaScript, it does not run at all on the standard adversarial input. The JavaScript realization must convert to an EXPLICIT STACK, which is materially harder than the recursion it replaces: post-order specifically requires either a two-phase visit marker or an iterator-position-per-node scheme, because a child's value must be folded into the parent AFTER all children are done. That conversion is a real acquisition a C++ learner never makes. A downstream agent that inherits the C++ default here ships an exercise that crashes.

Every site is classified **live / generated / historical** and treated by its class: a live claim is corrected, a generated one is **regenerated from an edited source**, a historical one is left standing because a narrative of what *was* true is not a false present-tense claim. **Limb 3 reached 10 files limb 1 did not** — canonically `../../C005-dp-progression/01_progression-stages.md`, which carries the stage distribution, the PS-4 share and the depth range while containing **zero** `F-943-` matches (`grep -c 'F-943-'` → **0**).
